title: Tanzanian Coconut Doughnut Balls
community: Zanzibar and the Swahili coast — the celebration doughnut
author: Chef Fatuma
desc: Tanzanian Kaimati — soft, round wheat dough balls deep-fried until golden, then drizzled with a sugar syrup infused with cardamom and rose water. Zanzibar's celebration sweet — soft inside, crispy outside, fragrant with rose and cardamom.
longDesc: Kaimati are one of Zanzibar's most beloved celebration sweets — soft dough balls fried until golden, then dipped while still hot into a rose water and cardamom sugar syrup that coats them in a fragrant, sticky glaze. They are made for Eid, for weddings, and for the most joyful occasions.
steps: Dissolve yeast and sugar in warm water. Rest 10 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour, cardamom, and salt. Add yeast mixture.
Mix to a soft, sticky batter — thicker than pancake, thinner than bread dough.
Cover and rest 60 minutes until bubbled and doubled.
Make syrup: boil sugar and water 5 minutes until slightly thickened. Add cardamom and rose water. Keep warm.
Drop tablespoons of batter into oil — they should be roughly round.
Fry 3—4 minutes, turning, until deeply golden all over.
Immediately dip hot kaimati in warm syrup. Toss to coat.
chefTips: Dip in syrup while hot — the syrup penetrates while the kaimati is still steaming.
The batter should be thick enough to hold its shape but soft enough to drop from a spoon.
Rose water is the Zanzibar signature — do not omit.
commonMistakes: Syrup too cold — does not penetrate.
cookingScience: When hot kaimati are dipped in warm syrup, the differential in temperature creates a brief suction effect as the interior cools — drawing the syrup into the surface of the dough. This is why dipping while hot produces a more evenly glazed result than dipping cold.
healthBenefits: Best enjoyed as a celebration treat.
culturalNote: Kaimati are Zanzibar's Eid sweet — made in enormous quantities for the celebration, shared with neighbours and the needy, and eaten with chai in the morning after prayers. The smell of rose water and cardamom signals the Eid morning more powerfully than anything else.
